question: Is the reconstructed ship motion the game's motion?
answer_note: The game was never run. No number in this report came from the running game. The divergence found below is between two reconstruction harnesses, tie-broken by the game's authored Lua data rather than by its runtime behaviour.

straight_line.verdict: agree to the logs' own rounding; covers the throttle gate, the 0092D300 acceleration selection, the target-speed product and the integration

cause.why: 0082ECB0 divides MaxRotAngle by the curve 0082E890 interpolates from the gameplay settings singleton [00F8753C] at +438h..+44Ch. The knots are authored in <install>/scripts/datatables/shipglobals.lua under ShipGlobals["Navigator"]["TurnMultipliers"], lines 340-342, and give 2.0 at full throttle. The probe reads them; bsp_game.exe still forces all three to 1.
cause.consequence: every milestone-2i heading and turning path is out by the denominator, measured as exactly 2.0 at full throttle; straight-line distances are unaffected

breakpoint.frame_delta: [ESP+4] as a float at entry, before the first instruction SUB ESP,0B0h runs
breakpoint.fires: once per ship per fixed step, for all 32 units; filter on the controlled unit's base pointer

derived.forward_speed: linear velocity projected on pose row 2
derived.yaw_rate: the angular velocity's row-1 component, which is what 0092E8C0 slews
derived.heading: atan2(fwd_x, fwd_z), derived by the tool and not captured

corrections.correction: one mutating Ghidra call was made in error: disassemble_bytes over 00826866..0082692F, 202 bytes. The range is already inside 00825F20's function body and the listing read back afterwards is unchanged; the program was not saved.

the probe no longer forces the rudder-curve knots to 1.0 and no longer uses a stand-in integrator; its header prints the shipglobals.lua knots and 'integration 00C41550 + 00C5B1B0, the game's own routines'. Only the ocean sampler and the gameplay scale remain stand-ins. Its uncertainty 3 likewise says 0082ECB0's settings block remains unrecovered; docs/UNIT_RUDDER_CURVE.md recovered it, on the settings singleton rather than on the unit.
annotated 'one store'; 00826A3A is FLD float ptr [ESI+9C0h], a load. unit+9C0h holds the unit's maximum speed and is the multiplicand. The product is stored to the stack at 00826A4F.

its stand-in note that the +438h..+44Ch knots 'were never recovered, so the three denominator knots are forced to 1 (the same stand-in src/ship_motion_probe.cpp uses)' is wrong in both halves. Every milestone-2i heading and turning path is out by the denominator, exactly 2.0 at full throttle. Its reported 0.06109 rad/s at rudder 0.5 reaches the right number for the wrong reason: MaxRotAngle * 0.5 with the knots forced to 1, where the shipped curve gives MaxRotAngle * 0.5 / 2.0 = 0.03054.

the 'expected yaw rate with the shipped curve' line omits the rudder factor: at --rudder 0.5 it prints 0.06109 rad/s against a measured 0.03054 and concludes 'heading turns at the curve's rate: no'. The measurement is right and the expectation is wrong. No C++ was changed in this packet.

the live run of the sampling plan, once a person can drive the menus to USN02. The two one-shot reads need only a main menu.
what the authored Cruise order writes into the ring. The live capture records it as a side effect; milestone 2i lists it as open, and the probe cannot reproduce the mission's ships without it.
already proposed by docs/UNIT_INSTANCE_UPDATE.md. This packet pinned the translation at +0FCh/+100h/+104h and the three basis rows from the keel-point arithmetic.
whether the shipped executable runs the x87 unit at 53-bit or 64-bit precision. docs/SHIP_MOTION.md calls this its first open question.

uncertainties: The packet's question is unanswered: no number here was taken from the running game. The harness divergence is tie-broken by the game's authored Lua, not by its runtime behaviour.

Whether the game applies the turn curve to the ordered throttle or to the achieved speed ratio. 0082ECB0 takes forwardSpeed / MaxSpeed; the Hungarian comment on the Lua knots says 'gazkar allasa', the throttle setting. The two agree in steady state and differ during the acceleration ramp, which is where the harnesses separate before t = 6 s.
The handedness of the body basis, unchanged from docs/SHIP_MOTION.md.
The x87 control word the shipped executable runs with, unchanged.

--align-origin assumes the capture and the probe start from rest on the same heading. A capture from a ship already under way needs its initial velocity fed to the probe, which the probe has no option for.
